title: Samuel
lead: The last of Israel's judges and the first of its great prophets after Moses, about 1050 BC: the son Hannah asked for, raised at Shiloh, who anointed Saul and then David as king.

sections.b: Samuel is born to the barren Hannah and given to the LORD at Shiloh (1 Samuel 1). As a boy he hears God call him by night (1 Samuel 3), and all Israel comes to know him as a prophet. He leads Israel to put away its idols and wins a victory at Mizpah (1 Samuel 7), judges Israel on a yearly circuit, and then, against his own wish, gives the people a king (1 Samuel 8–12). He anoints Saul, later rejects him (1 Samuel 15), and anoints David (1 Samuel 16). Even after his death he speaks once more, at Endor (1 Samuel 28). Jeremiah 15:1 and Psalm 99:6 name him with Moses as a man of prayer, 1 Chronicles 29:29 mentions records of "Samuel the seer," Acts 3:24 counts the prophets from Samuel on, and Hebrews 11:32 lists him among the heroes of faith.
